differentiation.occupancy_preservation: The loss applies a residual-conditioned tangential update to the source-selected codeword relative to the codebook centroid; the projection removes the residual-parallel component. The selected index is stop-gradient, and the update is anchored to the source-selected codeword rather than an attractive shared pair prototype, so it does not directly pull the transition's two endpoint codewords together. Indirect convergence through shared codeword updates remains possible and must be checked.

vs_r8.why: Unlike the inert encoder-only terms, it includes an explicit codebook path. Unlike the collapsed pairwise objective, it uses a residual-orthogonal, source-anchored transport signal rather than minimizing endpoint codeword distance or assigning both endpoints to one code. The projection and anchoring reduce direct pair convergence but do not rule out indirect codebook collapse, so the probe and frozen structural checks are essential.

differentiation.vs_reference_arm: the reference arm is the untouched host; this candidate adds one term whose gradient reaches the codebook without pulling a transition's two codewords together

equation: For each valid row i, let r_i = target_i - source_i, u_i = r_i / (||r_i|| + epsilon), and let c_i be the nearest codeword to source_i. Define v_i = codebook_{c_i} - mean_c(codebook_c), then q_i = v_i - (v_i dot u_i)u_i. Let L = -w * mean_i mask_i * (q_i dot (target_i - codebook_{c_i})).
expected_failure_modes: The tangential signal may be weak or noisy when residuals are small, and codewords selected by many transitions may drift together indirectly. It may also improve pair separation while damaging level-0 usage, prefix branching, frequency stability, or sequence information; no downstream benefit is assumed.

forbidden_substitutions.reason: a quota on the assignment is the family that produced 39.5% and 24.2% occupancy without preserving the exported codes
a term that pulls a pair's two codewords together is what collapsed the level-0 codebook to two codes

hypotheses: Reject if the checker finds a zero or nonfinite codebook gradient, if swapping source and target does not change the loss, or if the frozen evaluation violates any measured requirement (level-0 Gini no higher than control, at least control's L1-to-L2 branches per code, no greater train-to-test frequency drift, no lower sequence information) or fails to raise pair-level ER.

symbols.c_i: Nearest codeword index to source_i; treated as fixed for the loss.
symbols.epsilon: Small positive stabilizer for residual normalization.
symbols.mask_i: Validity indicator or weight for row i.
symbols.q_i: Component of v_i orthogonal to the transition residual direction.
symbols.r_i: Behaviour-conditioned residual vector from source to target.
symbols.source_i: Source embedding for transition row i.
symbols.target_i: Target embedding for transition row i.
symbols.u_i: Unit residual direction, stabilized by epsilon.
symbols.v_i: Selected source codeword relative to the codebook centroid.

tests.statement: the term's value on a hand-computable case matches the declared equation
the gradient reaches exactly the declared parameter groups

title: Behaviour-conditioned residual transport projected away from pair convergence
